items.item_text: Active, non-probationary California RN license.
Certification in Case Management (CCM or ACM); strongly preferred and considered a differentiating qualification for candidates seeking to lead this specialty.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Bachelor's degree in nursing or other healthcare profession, or a combination of comparable clinical education and / or experience.
Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA), Health Administration (MHA), Public Administration (MPA), or a closely related business/administration discipline strongly preferred.

A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible healthcare leadership experience, including substantial responsibility for care management, care transitions, post-acute services, social work, patient progression, or related clinical operations.
Experience overseeing post-acute networks, LTACH, SNF, inpatient rehabilitation, home health, hospice, or joint-venture/affiliate relationships.

At least five (5) years in senior leadership roles with accountability for leaders, multidisciplinary teams, budgets, and measurable operational outcomes in a complex hospital, academic medical center, integrated delivery network, or multi-site health system.
Experience integrating acute, ambulatory, home-based, population-health, and community-based care models.
Demonstrated experience using operational, clinical, and financial data to set strategy, manage performance, and achieve measurable improvements.
Experience in an academic medical center or large, multi-campus integrated health system.
Demonstrated experience managing budgets, workforce plans, vendor/partner relationships, and complex operational change.
Experience with value-based care, payer partnerships, risk arrangements, total-cost-of-care strategies, and population-health programs.
Experience with Epic or other enterprise EHR platforms and related care coordination, patient progression, and analytics capabilities.
Experience with hospice operations, GIP level of care, and/or home-based care models.

The Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), Care Transitions is the senior operational executive accountable for designing, integrating, and leading UC San Diego Health’s enterprise care-transitions strategy across Jacobs Medical Center, Hillcrest Medical Center, East Campus, and the affiliated post-acute networks. The CAO will lead a comprehensive redesign of care management and related transition services to ensure patients receive the right care, in the right setting, at the right time, with safe, timely, and financially sustainable transitions across the continuum.

The portfolio includes enterprise Care Management, Clinical Social Work, General Inpatient (GIP) Hospice operations, and the operational strategy, governance, performance management, and utilization of post-acute joint ventures, affiliates, contracted providers, and community-based resources. The CAO will also lead or coordinate enterprise home-health and other hospital-at-home transition programs where operational ownership resides within UC San Diego Health. The role will build a connected operating model spanning acute, post-acute, home-based, ambulatory, and community settings, in close partnership with Population Health, the Clinical Integration Network (CIN), physician leadership, nursing, finance, quality, revenue cycle, and external partners.

Serving as the senior operational dyad to the Associate Chief Medical Officer (aCMO), Acute and Post-Acute Care and Chief Medical Officer and Chief Operating Officer of Population Health and CIN, the CAO translates clinical strategy into enterprise operating models, measurable performance, and accountable execution. The position reports to the enterprise Chief Medical Officer (CMO).
Enterprise Scope and Reporting Relationships
Direct operational accountability across all three UC San Diego Health hospital campuses: Jacobs Medical Center, Hillcrest Medical Center, and East Campus.

Direct portfolio: enterprise Care Management; Clinical Social Work; GIP Hospice operations; post-acute network and partnership operations; and designated home-health, transitional-care, navigation, and community-connection programs.

The CAO owns care-transition execution and discharge/placement operations; a separate clinical utilization structure owns medical-necessity review, physician advisor practice, and clinical documentation improvement (CDI).

Establish shared governance with Palliative Care, hospice medical leadership, ambulatory care, home-based care, and community partners to ensure coordinated transitions without blurring clinical accountability.
1. Enterprise Strategy, Operating Model Design, and Transformation

Develop and execute a multi-year enterprise Care Transitions & Smart Navigation strategy aligned with UC San Diego Health’s clinical, access, quality, patient-experience, population-health, and financial priorities.

Redesign the end-to-end operating model for care management, social work, discharge planning, transitions, post-acute placement, and home-based services across all campuses and relevant ambulatory settings.

Establish a consistent enterprise model with clear decision rights, standard work, escalation pathways, service expectations, staffing models, span of control, and accountability while accommodating appropriate campus-level variation.
Lead complex, cross-functional transformation initiatives from strategy and business case through implementation, adoption, benefits realization, and sustainment.
Build a culture of proactive care progression, early discharge planning, interdisciplinary problem solving, patient and family partnership, and continuous improvement.
2. Care Management, Social Work, and Patient Progression

Provide executive oversight of enterprise inpatient and applicable ambulatory Care Management and Clinical Social Work operations, including staffing, productivity, professional practice interfaces, service standards, and performance.

Integrate case management, social work, discharge planning, complex-care coordination, and transition support into a coordinated model that addresses clinical, functional, behavioral, psychosocial, and social-needs barriers.
Establish early identification and risk stratification for patients likely to experience avoidable days, delayed discharge, readmission, avoidable admission, or complex post-acute needs.

Develop differentiated pathways for high-risk and high-need populations, including patients with complex placement needs, frequent utilization, limited community supports, and barriers to safe discharge.
Partner with nursing, physicians, therapy, pharmacy, and ancillary services to improve patient progression, timely decision-making, discharge readiness, and safe transitions.
3. Post-Acute Network, Joint Ventures, Affiliates, and Community Partnerships

Own the operational relationship and performance-management framework for UC San Diego Health’s post-acute joint ventures, affiliates, contracted providers, and strategic relationships, including LTACH, skilled nursing, inpatient rehabilitation, home health, hospice, and other applicable post-acute settings.

Establish enterprise governance, service-level expectations, referral and acceptance workflows, escalation processes, quality and safety expectations, data-sharing standards, and performance scorecards for post-acute partners in collaboration with Strategy and other relevant stakeholders.

Partner with supply chain, legal, finance, compliance, clinical leadership, and network development to evaluate partner performance, capacity, access, financial arrangements, strategic fit, and opportunities to expand or redesign the network.
Optimize appropriate utilization of internal and external post-acute resources, balancing patient choice, clinical appropriateness, quality, access, capacity, total cost of care, and continuity.
Strengthen community connections and resource pathways, including 211 and other community-based organizations, to address social needs and reduce avoidable acute-care utilization.
4. Home-Based Care and Transitional Programs

Where assigned, provide operational oversight and strategic integration of home-health programs and hospital-to-home transition services, including post-discharge follow-up, home-based support, and transitional care models.
Partner with Population Health, CIN, ambulatory operations, primary care, and specialty care to connect hospital-based transitions with longitudinal care management and value-based care programs.
Develop scalable pathways that support safe care at home, reduce avoidable ED visits and admissions, improve post-discharge follow-up, and strengthen continuity across settings.
Coordinate with UC San Diego Health at Home, remote patient monitoring, virtual care, and other digital programs to define referral criteria, workflows, accountability, and measurable outcomes.
5. Hospice and Complex Supportive Care

Provide operational oversight of GIP Hospice services, including access, patient flow, staffing, financial performance, quality, regulatory readiness, and coordination with hospice medical leadership.
Establish reliable operational interfaces with inpatient Palliative Care, outpatient palliative services, hospice, social work, and community-based supportive care.

Partner with the CMO and aCMO to ensure clinical governance and professional practice for Palliative Care remain clearly defined; operational integration should not compromise physician-led clinical accountability.
6. Population Health, CIN, and Avoidable Utilization

Co-develop care-transition pathways with Population Health and the CIN that connect inpatient discharge planning to ambulatory follow-up, longitudinal care management, community services, and value-based care arrangements.
Develop operating models to reduce preventable readmissions, avoidable admissions, ED utilization, unnecessary days, and preventable post-acute utilization.
Create targeted interventions for high-risk cohorts and frequent utilizers, with clear attribution, handoffs, escalation, and outcome measurement across the enterprise.
Align transition strategies with payer, risk-contract, quality, access, and total-cost-of-care objectives without creating inappropriate barriers to clinically necessary care.
7. Performance Management, Analytics, Digital Enablement, and AI
Establish an enterprise performance system with transparent dashboards, operational reviews, campus and service-line accountability, and routine executive reporting.
Use clinical, operational, financial, and patient-experience data to identify variation, forecast demand, prioritize interventions, and evaluate outcomes.

Partner with Information Services, analytics, digital health, and clinical informatics to define requirements and implement decision support, predictive analytics, machine learning, workflow automation, and AI-enabled tools that improve care management effectiveness and workforce capacity.
Ensure technology investments are grounded in a clear operating model, workflow redesign, adoption plan, measurable benefits, data governance, privacy, safety, and responsible-use standards.
Lead Lean-based improvement and benefits realization, including sustainment of gains and transparent reporting of realized results.
8. Financial, Workforce, and Governance Accountability
Own portfolio budgeting, financial planning, productivity, staffing strategy, resource allocation, and business-case development.

Establish partner-level and enterprise-level financial and operational accountability for post-acute utilization, avoidable days, length of stay, readmissions, discharge efficiency, and total cost of care.
Develop a high-performing leadership team with clear succession plans, leadership development, role clarity, and a strong culture of accountability and collaboration.
Represent the portfolio in executive committees, clinical and operational governance forums, joint-venture governance, and strategic planning processes.
Risk-adjusted 7-, 30-, and 90-day readmissions and potentially preventable readmissions.Potentially avoidable admissions, ED revisits, and utilization among targeted high-risk populations.
Length of stay, excess days, avoidable days, discharge order-to-departure time, discharge-before-noon where clinically appropriate, and discharge predictability.
Time from medical readiness to post-acute placement; referral-to-acceptance and acceptance-to-transfer intervals; placement denials and barriers.
Post-acute utilization by setting, partner, quality, patient outcomes, access, total cost, and readmission performance.
Home-health referral acceptance, start-of-care timeliness, completed post-discharge outreach, follow-up completion, and escalation outcomes.
Patient/family experience, transition communication, medication reconciliation and follow-up reliability, equity of access, and complaints.
Care Management and Social Work productivity, caseload acuity, staffing effectiveness, turnover, engagement, and service responsiveness.
GIP Hospice access, census, length of stay, quality, patient/family experience, and financial performance.
Realized financial impact, including avoidable utilization reduction, capacity recapture, cost per case, and partner/network value.
Demonstrated success leading enterprise or multi-campus redesign of care management, discharge planning, transitions of care, or post-acute operations.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or higher; Black Belt preferred.
Demonstrated success leading complex departmental and interdepartmental projects, including business case development, change management, implementation, and benefits realization.

Demonstrated success identifying, designing, and operationalizing digital decision support, predictive analytics, machine learning, workflow automation, or AI-enabled tools in care management or care transitions.
Demonstrated ability to lead across clinical and administrative disciplines, influence physician and executive stakeholders, and deliver results in a matrixed environment.
